## What it shows

These figures come from my work on Abe Genki (安倍源基), the former head of the Special Higher Police (Tokkō) and Japan's last wartime Home Minister. In January 1958 Abe became a representative director of the Shin Nippon Kyōgi Kai (新日本協議会), the Council for a New Japan, a national anti-communist organisation whose doctrinal manifesto was *Daisan no michi* (第三の道, *The Third Way*).

Figure 1 maps the Council's organisation around 1958–59 from the officer roster printed in *Daisan no michi*. Directors are grouped by the intellectual or institutional tradition they brought with them, alongside the Council's funding, publications and the wider right-wing milieu it drew on.

Figure 2 sets out four transwar trajectories, those of Abe Genki, Rōyama Masamichi, Nishio Suehiro and Nabeyama Sadachika, which began in very different places in interwar political thought and ended at the same organicist anthropology set out in *Daisan no michi*.

## How to use it

1. Click any box in either figure. A panel below the figure explains who or what it is and its place in the argument.
2. In Figure 1, the box for the 20 further directors lists the rest of the roster.
3. A dagger (†) marks identifications that still need to be verified.

## Sources

Officer roster printed in *Daisan no michi: hon-kai no shidō rinen* (Shin Nippon Kyōgi Kai, 1959), 42. Secondary literature including Large (1976), Mimura (2011), Hofmann (2020) and Starrs (2023).
